candidates.tagline: OpenAI built a $230 keyboard so you can boss around your AI coding agents
candidates.story: OpenAI launched its first-ever hardware product on July 15, 2026 — the Codex Micro, a $230 macro pad co-designed with Work Louder, featuring light-up 'Agent Keys' that glow different colors to show whether AI coding agents are idle, working, done, or erroring, plus a joystick and a dial to adjust AI 'reasoning' levels.
candidates.why_funny: The company whose AI assistants are supposed to replace programmers just shipped a $230 specialized device to help programmers more efficiently supervise their AI assistants.
candidates.alt: The OpenAI Codex Micro — a compact square macro pad with 13 illuminated mechanical keys in a dark housing, a rotary dial, small joystick, and color-coded LED status lights showing Codex agent states — displayed against a dark background with the OpenAI branding visible

candidates.tagline: Google's CEO said 'give us a month' for Gemini. He said it three times.
candidates.story: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro — announced at Google I/O in May 2026, with CEO Sundar Pichai telling a visibly frustrated crowd of developers 'Give us until next month to get it to you' — has since missed its promised June launch and its rescheduled July 17 target, making it the most publicly broken tech promise of the year.
candidates.why_funny: The CEO of the world's most powerful search and AI infrastructure company promised his flagship model three times and missed all three, while rival models GPT-5.6 and Grok 4.5 already shipped.
candidates.alt: Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet, on stage at the Google I/O developer conference at Moscone Center in San Francisco, presenting to a packed auditorium of developers with the Google I/O stage backdrop and lighting visible behind him
